moveEvidence.claimSummary: Licona's appeal to divine intention is circular, and resurrection requires evidence comparable to other wholly unconfirmed extraordinary claims.
moveEvidence.reasonSummary: Whether an intending God acted is the point needing proof; unlike ordinary possessions, divine appearances and bodily resurrection lack established instances, so much stronger evidence is required.

inferenceSummary.premise: The proposed intention is not independently established and the event type lacks confirmed background instances.
inferenceSummary.inference: Intention cannot raise the probability without assuming the disputed supernatural framework.
inferenceSummary.conclusion: The available historical evidence does not overcome the resurrection claim's very low prior.

moveEvidence.importanceRationale: This is the clearest methodological disagreement over how miracle claims can be historically supported.

responseComponents.description: Argues divine intention cannot be used before supernatural action is evidenced.
